content: Elafibranor is indicated for the treatment of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) in adults. It is used in combination with ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) for patients who have had an inadequate response to UDCA or as monotherapy in patients unable to tolerate UDCA. The recommended dose is 80 mg orally once daily. The safety and efficacy of elafibranor have not been fully established. Drug Interactions: 1. Elafibranor and Atorvastatin: Co-administration may increase the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Both drugs elevate the risk of creatine phosphokinase (CPK) elevation and/or myalgia. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Elafibranor and Cholestyramine: Cholestyramine reduces elafibranor levels by binding the drug in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer elafibranor at least 4 hours before or after taking bile acid-binding sequestrants, or at the longest interval possible. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 3. Elafibranor and Colesevelam: Colesevelam decreases elafibranor levels through drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer elafibranor at least 4 hours before or after bile acid-binding sequestrants. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 4. Elafibranor and Colestipol: Colestipol reduces elafibranor levels by binding the drug in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer elafibranor at least 4 hours before or after bile acid-binding sequestrants. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 5. Elafibranor and Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Elafibranor decreases the levels or effects of these hormonal contraceptives by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Switch to effective non-hormonal contraceptives or add a barrier method during elafibranor treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. Monitor closely. 6. Elafibranor and Drospirenone: Elafibranor reduces the levels or effects of drospirenone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use effective non-hormonal contraceptives or add a barrier method during treatment and for 3 weeks after the last dose. Monitor closely. 7. Elafibranor and Ethinylestradiol: Elafibranor decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Switch to non-hormonal contraceptives or add a barrier method during treatment and for 3 weeks after the last dose. Monitor closely. 8. Elafibranor and Fluvastatin: Co-administration increases the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Both drugs elevate the risk of CPK elevation and/or myalgia. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Elafibranor and Levonorgestrel (oral or transdermal): Elafibranor reduces the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use effective non-hormonal contraceptives or add a barrier method during treatment and for 3 weeks after the last dose. Monitor closely. 10. Elafibranor and Lovastatin: Co-administration increases the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Both drugs elevate the risk of CPK elevation and/or myalgia. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Elafibranor and Norgestrel: Elafibranor decreases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use effective non-hormonal contraceptives or add a barrier method during treatment and for 3 weeks after the last dose. Monitor closely. 12. Elafibranor and Pitavastatin: Co-administration increases the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Both drugs elevate the risk of CPK elevation and/or myalgia. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Elafibranor and Pravastatin: Co-administration increases the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Both drugs elevate the risk of CPK elevation and/or myalgia. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Elafibranor and Rifampin: Rifampin decreases elafibranor levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Elafibranor and Rosuvastatin: Co-administration increases the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Both drugs elevate the risk of CPK elevation and/or myalgia. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Elafibranor and Simvastatin: Co-administration increases the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Both drugs elevate the risk of CPK elevation and/or myalgia. Use caution and monitor closely. Adverse Reactions: Common adverse effects include weight gain (23%), diarrhea (11%), abdominal pain (11%), nausea (11%), vomiting (11%), arthralgia (8%), constipation (8%), muscle pain (7%), fractures (6%), gastroesophageal reflux disease (6%), dry mouth (5%), weight loss (5%), rash (5%), dizziness (≤5%), gastroenteritis (≤5%), increased blood creatinine (≤5%), anemia (≤5%), CPK elevation >3x ULN (4%), myalgia (4%), cholelithiasis (3%), and combined CPK elevation with myalgia (1%). Rare but serious adverse effects include rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury (1%). Pregnancy and Lactation: Based on animal reproduction studies, elafibranor may cause fetal harm when administered during pregnancy. There is insufficient data from human pregnancies to assess the risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. Verify a negative pregnancy test before initiating treatment in females of reproductive potential. Report pregnancies to Ipsen Pharmaceuticals. Data on the presence of elafibranor or its metabolites in human or animal milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its effects on milk production are unavailable. Due to the potential for serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants, patients should not breastfeed during treatment and for 3 weeks after the last dose. Pharmacokinetics: Elafibranor is extensively metabolized to form a major active metabolite (GFT1007) via cytosolic enzyme 15-ketoprostaglandin 13-reductase (PTGR1). GFT1007 is further metabolized by CYP2C8, UGT1A3, and UGT2B7. Elafibranor is also metabolized by CYP2J2 and UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT) isoforms UGT1A3, UGT1A4, and UGT2B7. Volume of distribution (Vd): 4,731 L. Total clearance: 50 L/hr. May be taken with or without food. Storage: Store at 15–30°C (59–86°F) in the original package (bottle and carton) to protect from moisture and light.
